decisions.decision: Make the threshold crossing and descent into the underground gallery HELIOT's primary signature moment.
whyLadder: Creative: the threshold is the only moment that transforms the browser from a viewing surface into an entered place.
Brand: HELIOT's truth is that light becomes architecture and interaction rather than decorative image-making.
Audience: design-literate visitors need proof that the immersive claim is spatial, not merely visual.
Emotional: anticipation becomes awe when the exterior disappears behind physical architecture.
Medium: scroll naturally maps to continuous authored travel and reverse reconstruction.
Production: the current world, passage and camera path already support the move with validated physical clearance.

rejectedAlternatives.decision: Use the late aerial orbit as the main signature.
rejectedAlternatives.reason: It is visually strong but less ownable and less conceptually tied to physical entry than the threshold descent.

rejectedAlternatives.decision: Use an exploded instrument assembly as the main signature.
rejectedAlternatives.reason: It would collapse HELIOT back into familiar product-visualization language and compete with the architectural idea.

decisions.author: forge-director

decisions.decision: Quiet fixed UI chrome during threshold alignment and descent, then restore it as the experience shifts back toward explanation and utility.
whyLadder: Creative: silence creates contrast and gives the primary spatial move visual authority.
Brand: HELIOT should feel architectural and measured rather than interface-heavy.
Audience: fewer simultaneous signals make the physical transition easier to understand.
Emotional: reduced interface noise increases anticipation and release.
Medium: CSS state can respond directly to the active chapter without changing the semantic document.
Production: the root already exposes chapter state, so the final-cut treatment is low-risk and reversible.

rejectedAlternatives.decision: Hide all interface for the entire experience.
rejectedAlternatives.reason: That would weaken chapter orientation, accessibility and the field-instrument character outside the signature moment.

decisions.author: forge-director

decisions.decision: Keep manual orbit confined to the inspection chapter and reset it before authored travel resumes.
whyLadder: Creative: directed cinematography and exploratory inspection serve different jobs and should not blur together.
Brand: HELIOT is an authored observatory journey, not an unrestricted model viewer.
Audience: visitors receive agency exactly where close inspection has value.
Emotional: agency arrives after understanding and before the return flight.
Medium: the existing orbit store already supports scoped control and reset.
Production: confining manual state protects deterministic reverse scroll and camera continuity.

rejectedAlternatives.decision: Allow free orbit throughout all ten chapters.
rejectedAlternatives.reason: It would undermine authored framing, spatial safety and the meaning of the threshold route.

decisions.author: forge-director

decisions.decision: Treat the light laboratory as causal interaction: aperture must change geometry, rays, readout and saved artifact together.
whyLadder: Creative: interaction is meaningful only when it changes the actual world or what the visitor takes away.
Brand: revealing the unseen requires demonstrating the consequences of changing light.
Audience: technical and design-literate visitors can distinguish real system behavior from decorative controls.
Emotional: understanding becomes agency when the visitor sees several representations respond together.
Medium: browser state can synchronize WebGL, semantic UI and downloadable output in real time.
Production: the shared light-lab store already connects these surfaces deterministically.

rejectedAlternatives.reason: That would convert a proof point into a cosmetic gimmick.

decisions.author: forge-director

decisions.decision: Keep the late aerial reveal as a secondary resolution rather than a second climax.
whyLadder: Creative: one unmistakable peak makes the overall experience more memorable than multiple competing peaks.
Brand: the aerial should reveal how the observatory belongs to the field, not advertise spectacle for its own sake.
Audience: after moving through the interior, visitors benefit from seeing the whole spatial relationship in context.
Emotional: awe has already peaked; the aerial delivers admiration and cognitive resolution.
Medium: a calmer camera crane can reinterpret previously experienced geometry without introducing a new interaction language.
Production: the existing path already provides the shot, so restraint is primarily a direction and pacing decision.

rejectedAlternatives.decision: Escalate the aerial reveal beyond the threshold descent with stronger orbit, bloom or speed.
rejectedAlternatives.reason: That would flatten the intensity curve and make the primary signature less unique.

decisions.author: forge-director

decisions.decision: Preserve mobile, reduced-motion and no-WebGL states as the same idea expressed with less spectacle, not as lesser concepts.
whyLadder: Creative: the concept is threshold, light and evidence—not desktop-only movement.
Brand: a disciplined flagship should remain coherent when the rendering mode changes.
Audience: visitors on constrained devices still deserve narrative and functional completeness.
Emotional: the sequence can retain curiosity, understanding and ownership even when motion is reduced.
Medium: semantic document structure, static fallback imagery and wider mobile camera framing provide alternate expressions of the same story.
Production: existing fallback, reduced-motion and mobile code paths already make this achievable without separate content architecture.

rejectedAlternatives.decision: Serve a simplified marketing page on mobile or fallback.
rejectedAlternatives.reason: That would abandon the core concept instead of translating it.

decisions.author: forge-director
